comments.title: Preserve and verify worktree lock metadata
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve and verify worktree lock metadata**

In the fixture's locked `echo` case, running `git worktree unlock` and then performing the expected removals still makes this checker return `ok`, because `listed_worktrees()` discards every porcelain field except the path. This allows the trial to pass after silently removing the lock that protects an active worktree, contrary to the cleanup safety behavior being evaluated; record the expected lock state/reason and compare it during `check()`.

comments.title: Prevent stale-lock takeover from replacing a new owner
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent stale-lock takeover from replacing a new owner**

On POSIX, `rename(claim, path)` replaces an existing destination. Because the preceding rename temporarily removes `.orch.lock`, another process can successfully acquire it with `open(path, "wx")` during that gap; this rename then silently overwrites the new process's lock, and both processes proceed believing they have exclusive access to the TSV store. Install the claim with a non-replacing operation or revalidate ownership so a writer that acquires during the takeover wins exclusively.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

comments.title: Close the third-writer gap in lock takeover
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Close the third-writer gap in lock takeover**

When three processes contend for a stale lock, contender A can install its claim, B can rename A's lock while detecting an identity mismatch, and C can create a new lock during that gap. This catch then preserves C and removes A's moved lock, but A has already succeeded and never rechecks ownership, leaving A and C able to write the store concurrently. The takeover needs serialization or another mechanism that cannot expose an unlocked gap while displacing a successful owner.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

comments.title: Avoid replacing a successor lock during takeover
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid replacing a successor lock during takeover**

During a forced takeover, a live holder can release the observed lock after the inode check, allowing a normal writer to create a successor before this replacing `rename`. The rename then silently overwrites that successor while it remains in its critical section, and the force caller also proceeds, breaking store mutual exclusion and risking corrupted state. Use a takeover protocol that preserves the identity check through the replacement operation.

comments.title: Do not retry terminal blocker codes unconditionally
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not retry terminal blocker codes unconditionally**

This requires correcting and relaunching every blocked charter, including `budget` and `non pris en charge`, even though those codes commonly have no in-session remedy; it also conflicts with the shared runtime rule in `runtime/suivi.md`, which retries only an identifiable temporary transport or availability failure and treats permission or capacity refusal as immediately blocked. Separate recoverable blockers from terminal ones and retain the latter in the final coverage gaps instead of creating an unbounded or impossible retry.

comments.title: Keep lower recommendations below the selected budget cap
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep lower recommendations below the selected budget cap**

When the user selects `réduit` and accepts the Development or Code review recommendation, this rule replaces the recommended `low` effort with `medium`, even though the scale immediately defines `medium > low`; consequently the reduced budget consumes more reasoning than `illimité`, which preserves the original `low` recommendation. Apply the selected effort as a ceiling—retain an existing lower recommendation rather than always fixing every explicit selection to the target.

comments.title: Serialize start-marker checks with concurrent writers
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize start-marker checks with concurrent writers**

When two executions append concurrently, one can inspect the tail, see no intervening writer, and then append a normal row after the other execution has inserted its `start` row. It has followed this read-before-write instruction, but the segmentation rule below now attributes its row to the other execution, corrupting the per-execution audit boundary. The tail check and append need an atomic lock/CAS protocol, or each row must carry its execution identity so ownership does not depend on race-prone ordering.

comments.title: Prevent new loop IDs from resetting a target's budget
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent new loop IDs from resetting a target's budget**

When a loop has consumed an attempt without progress, the caller can open another loop with a different ID but the same target and findings because collision detection considers only `next.id`. The second loop then accepts the same strategy content and starts with a fresh limit, allowing repeated correction dispatches that the first loop would reject; the original loop can later use its remaining attempt to complete, so checking all loops at delivery does not preserve the intended dispatch bound. Reject or explicitly link overlapping active loops for the same correction target so their attempt and strategy history cannot be reset by renaming the loop.
